## Overview

In this quickstart, you will start a real Fiber node inside a React page,
connect it to Fiber Testnet over WebSocket Secure, and read live node state.
The application uses Fiber WASM workers and stores its local node state in
IndexedDB.

This minimal node connection does not need an application backend. A
receiving service becomes useful when your product needs to issue invoices,
verify merchant payments, persist shared business data, or unlock server-side
content.

## 1. Create the React app

Create a Next.js application and install the Fiber browser SDK:

```bash
npm create next-app@latest fiber-hello
cd fiber-hello
npm install @fiber-pay/sdk
```

## 2. Enable browser isolation

Fiber WASM uses workers and `SharedArrayBuffer`. Add COOP and COEP response
headers to the route that runs the node:

```js
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  transpilePackages: [
    '@fiber-pay/sdk',
    '@nervosnetwork/fiber-js',
  ],
  async headers() {
    return [{
      source: '/fiber',
      headers: [
        {
          key: 'Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy',
          value: 'same-origin',
        },
        {
          key: 'Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy',
          value: 'require-corp',
        },
      ],
    }];
  },
};

export default nextConfig;
```

Check `crossOriginIsolated` before creating a browser node.

When this route is opened through client-side documentation navigation, the
new response headers cannot affect the already-loaded document. Detect that
case and perform one full-page reload so the browser can apply COOP and COEP.
The interactive preview on this page does this automatically.

## 3. Start Fiber WASM

Import `FiberBrowserNode` and `RawKeyCredentialProvider` from
`@fiber-pay/sdk/browser`. Create a Testnet credential, start the node, and make
an outbound WSS connection to a browser-reachable public Fiber peer.

Persist the same browser identity between sessions if the node will own
channels or payment state. Production apps also need encrypted key storage,
backup, account switching, and recovery.

```ts
const {
  FiberBrowserNode,
  RawKeyCredentialProvider,
} = await import('@fiber-pay/sdk/browser');

const credential = new RawKeyCredentialProvider(
  crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32)),
  crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32)),
  crypto.randomUUID(),
);

const node = new FiberBrowserNode({
  network: 'testnet',
  credential,
  nodeConfig: {
    bootnodes: [],
    logLevel: 'info',
  },
});

await node.start();
```

At this point the Fiber WASM node is running locally, but it is not connected
to the public peer. Connect only after the user explicitly requests it:

```ts
await node.connectPeer({
  address: routerWssMultiaddr.replace(/\/p2p\/[^/]+$/, ''),
  pubkey: routerPubkey,
});
```

## 4. Wire it into React

### 4.1 Keep the node between renders

Store the node in a ref and keep status, pubkey, and peer count in React state.

### 4.2 Start the WASM node

The first button starts Fiber and calls `getNodeInfo()`. It does not make a
network connection.

### 4.3 Connect only when requested

Enable a second button after the node starts. Connect to the public peer from
that handler, then query the peer list:

```ts
await node.connectPeer({ address: routerAddress, pubkey: routerPubkey });
const peerList = await node.listPeers();
setPeers(peerList.peers.length);
```

The interactive preview on this page runs this flow with a browser-local
Testnet identity and a public Testnet peer.
